messages.content:
RoadDraft is a headless 2D CAD engine for roadway plans. Model space is US survey feet, and a point is [x, y] = [easting, northing] -- the other way round from how coordinates are usually spoken, so N 7300, E 4100 is [4100, 7300]. Sheets are paper inches seen through viewports at a feet-per-inch scale. Work through the commands: each one validates its params and explains what was wrong, every change is journaled and undoable. Start with get_document_state to see what is in the document, list_commands for the full surface, and render_sheet or render_model to look at your work.

To annotate something, find it before you point at it. In a sheet file the design usually lives in a referenced basefile, so the document owns no geometry of its own; find_entities searches the attachments too. Filter by what a thing IS -- layer, type, or its design anchor -- rather than dumping the document: find_entities {anchor: {kind: 'offset', offset: [-15, 15]}, visible_on: 'P-202'} is the pavement edges that sheet shows. Then pass the id straight to place_callout as target_entity, and the engine puts the leader tip on the geometry. Do not compute the point yourself: the midpoint of a curve's endpoints is not on the curve, and roadway linework runs parallel a few feet apart, so a hand-computed point usually lands on the wrong line rather than on nothing. If you do pass a raw target point, read the warning that comes back -- it names what the tip actually touched.

Some things are not entities at all -- a station, a PC, a point at an offset. Ask the design for those: list_alignments with include_references=true names a referenced alignment 'BASE:RTE-7', and station_to_xy, xy_to_station, resolve_anchor and get_design_data all accept that name and answer in host coordinates. To call one out, give place_callout a target_anchor ('86+50@15R', 'PC-2'; BC-2 and EC-2 name the PC and PT too) and that alignment name. Otherwise commands do not take it: nothing can be drawn, labelled or anchored to an alignment this document does not own.

Plan annotation belongs on the sheet, in paper inches, not in the model. Pass the sheet as place_callout's space and still name a model target -- target_entity or target_anchor: the engine sees it through the sheet's viewport (scale and twist included) and puts the tip where it shows on the paper. 'at' then runs along the part of the entity that sheet shows, since a pavement edge runs the whole project and a sheet shows one stretch. find_entities with visible_on gives each row a sheet_point, which is where that tip will land -- use it to choose a position for the text that is clear of the linework. Never work out a viewport by hand: model_to_sheet and sheet_to_model convert, and station_to_xy and point_on_entity take a sheet and answer in paper inches as well.

Drafting from a description works the same way: give the engine the description, not coordinates you worked out. A bearing and distance goes in as written -- create_alignment takes start + legs (each leg a bearing, azimuth or deflection and the distance to the next PI, with the radius of the curve at the PI it starts from), draw_traverse draws lines and curves course by course, and traverse computes the points without drawing. offset_entity copies linework parallel at a distance (one entity, or a chain offset as one path), fillet rounds the corner between two lines with a curve (a curb return), and measure with along gives distances along a line, chain or alignment and square off it. key_points and snap give the exact endpoints, intersections, centers and alignment design points (PI, BC, EC) to build on. Station-and-offset drafting is draw_station_offset with the stations and offsets given ('82+00@15R'). Linework drawn through something is cut back with trim (a point on the part to cut away) or run on with extend, not redrawn from computed points; break, join, lengthen, chamfer, copy, rotate, mirror, scale and array edit what is there. create_points sets COGO points, label_segments letters bearings and distances or L1/C1 tags with line and curve tables, place_along sets blocks or points at an interval, hatch fills an area (a point inside is enough), and area and get_entity read areas, lengths, bearings and curve data off the drawing.

Do one drafting task in a headless CAD engine called RoadDraft, using the tools you have been given. They are your ENTIRE tool surface.

Rules:
- Every change to the drawing must go through a tool call.
- The document is already open and saves itself after each command. Do not save it under another name.
- Nobody can answer questions. Work until you judge the task done, then stop and give your report.
- You have no calculator and no code execution. Any arithmetic you need, do yourself.

THE TASK:
Add a right-turn lane to SR-100, on the right side: 12 ft wide, full width from station 31+20 to station 36+00, opened by a 120 ft straight taper that leaves the existing edge of pavement at station 30+00. Draw the new edge of pavement on layer rd_EP -- the taper, the full-width edge, and a square end at 36+00 back to the existing edge.

When finished, reply briefly with:
1. What you created and drew (names, layers, key coordinates).
2. The tool calls that mattered, in order (tool name + the key arguments).
3. Anything that failed, confused you, or that you had to work around -- quote error messages. If you had to compute coordinates yourself, show the arithmetic.

messages.reasoning:
Let's start by understanding the document's state.

Task: Add a right-turn lane on the right side of SR-100:
- 12 feet wide
- Full width from station 31+20 to station 36+00
- A 120-foot straight taper that departs from the existing edge of pavement at station 30+00
- Draw the new edge of pavement on layer rd_EP: the taper, the full-width edge, and a square end returning to the existing edge at 36+00.

So the turn lane's offset is 12 feet to the right of the existing EOP. The existing EOP is probably at some offset (e.g., 15 feet or 18 feet from the centerline). The turn lane edge will be at an offset of (existing EOP offset + 12).

Points (station, offset), relative to the alignment:
- 30+00 @ existing EOP offset (taper starting point)
- 31+20 @ existing EOP + 12 (120-foot taper: 30+00 to 31+20 = 120 feet)
- 36+00 @ existing EOP + 12 (full width)
- 36+00 @ existing EOP offset (square end returning to the existing edge)
- Close the shape? The task says "the taper, the full-width edge, and a square end returning to the existing edge at 36+00."

The shape is defined by 3 offset points: 30+00@0 (relative to EOP), 31+20@12, 36+00@12, 36+00@0, and back to 30+00@0 (along the existing EOP). Actually, draw_station_offset with points ['30+00@15R', '31+20@27R', '36+00@27R', '36+00@15R'] draws lines between them; the last leg from 36+00@15R back to 30+00@15R is not drawn unless close=true (in which case it closes to the first point, i.e., 30+00@15R). The existing EOP is presumably already drawn, so that side is covered. But should I close it? The task says to draw "the taper, the full-width edge, and a square end returning to the existing edge at 36+00." That's 3 segments: taper (30+00@15 to 31+20@27), full width (31+20@27 to 36+00@27), square end (36+00@27 to 36+00@15). So 3 segments, no close. But maybe closing would be fine/harmless? If close=true, a line overlapping the existing EOP between 30+00 and 36+00 gets added — not desired, could cause confusion. I'll go with 3 segments, no close.

First I need to find the alignment. Let's check the document state. SR-100 is probably an alignment named something like "RTE-100" or "SR-100".

The existing EOP offset is also needed. Typically, it's drawn at ±15 or ±18. I can find it with find_entities using an anchor with kind offset, or check the model state.

Plan:
1. get_document_state summary + list_alignments (include_references).
2. Find the existing EOP entity to determine the offset (find_entities anchor kind=offset, or get_design_data).
3. Confirm the stations exist (30+00, 31+20, 36+00 within the alignment's range).
4. Create layer rd_EP (color probably yellow or black; Caltrans plans often use black... use the default black, or check existing conventions; the task only specifies the layer name).
5. Use draw_station_offset with alignment, points ['30+00@<ep>R', '31+20@<ep+12>R', '36+00@<ep+12>R', '36+00@<ep>R'], layer rd_EP.
6. Verify with get_entity / render_model.

Note: draw_station_offset with follow=true: between points at the same offset, it follows the alignment (arc on curves) — that's fine for the full-width segment if there's a curve in between; if the offset changes, it's a straight-line taper. Good.

But wait — "full width from station 31+20 to station 36+00" — the full-width segment follows the alignment exactly at offset 27 (if EOP is 15). Even if there's a curve between 31+20 and 36+00, following the alignment is the correct drafting behavior (a turn lane follows the road). Good.

Also, confirm that the turn lane is "on the right side" — yes, positive offset.

Potential issue: the existing EOP might not be a design-offset line but drawn linework. If the EOP is an anchored offset entity, find_entities anchor {kind:'offset', offset:[15,15]} will find it. If it's just linework, I'll need to find which offset it's at — probably via xy_to_station on a point on the EOP, or by checking its position.

Let's start with parallel calls: get_document_state and list_alignments with references.

The document has an alignment called "SR-100" in the range 10+00 to 56+75.25. The layer rd_EP already exists. Task: add a right-turn lane on the right side:
- 12 feet wide (offset from the existing pavement edge: 15 to 27, or if the pavement is 30 feet wide with the edge at 15 feet, the turn lane extends from the existing EOP (edge of pavement) at offset 15R to 27R).

Wait — I need to know the offset of the existing pavement edge. The task says "a 120-foot straight taper departing from the existing pavement edge at station 30+00." So the taper begins from the existing EOP at 30+00 and reaches 12 feet offset over 120 feet. After that, the full 12-foot width continues from 31+20 to 36+00. And at 36+00 a square end back to the existing pavement edge.

So, I need to find the offset of the existing EOP on SR-100. Let me check the design data and the entities drawn on the rd_EP layer.

Let me look at the entities on the rd_EP layer and the alignment's tangents/curves to understand the geometry around stations 30+00 to 36+00.

messages.content: I've mapped the design: the SR-100 alignment has T-2 (a straight tangent) covering stations 27+91.37 → 40+31.72, so all three key stations (30+00, 31+20, 36+00) fall on the straight. The existing right EP is at offset +12 (chain LN-007/AR-005/LN-008/AR-006/LN-009). A new lane needs an edge that's at +12 up to 30+00, tapers to +24 at 31+20, runs full width at +24 to 36+00, and then drops vertically (perpendicular) back to +12. Let me verify the geometry against the existing EP line, and then draw it using station-offset points.
messages.reasoning:
Alright, let me understand the layout.

- Alignment SR-100: begins at station 10+00 (1000.0 ft), ends at 56+75.25.
- T-1: from [1000, 1000] to [2405.27, 1000], eastward, azimuth 90.
- C-1: left curve, R=1200, PC at 24+05.27, PT at 27+91.37.
- T-2: from [2784.74, 1061.58] to [3961.44, 1453.81], azimuth 71.565°.
- C-2: right curve R=900, PC at 40+31.72, PT at 43+21.30.
- T-3: from [4246.05, 1500] to [5600, 1500].

The existing edge of pavement on the right side of the direction of stationing is the offset -12 (right is negative? The task says "offset from the alignment, in feet, positive on the right of the stationing direction"). Wait, in the anchor of LN-004 it's offset -12.0 on T-1 — LN-004 is at y=1012 (north side), LN-007 is at y=988 (south side). The road runs east. Right of the eastbound direction is south. So the right edge is the offset -12 line at y=988? Hmm, wait: "positive on the right of the stationing direction". If right is positive, the right edge should be +12, not -12. But LN-004 (the north side, y=1012) has offset -12. So left is positive? That's contradictory.

Wait a moment. For T-1, the direction is east (azimuth 90). North of the line is the left side (if facing east, left is north). LN-004 at y=1012 is north = left, and its anchor offset is -12.0. LN-007 at y=988 is south = right, and its offset is +12.0. So here positive offset is on the right. OK, this matches: "offset in feet, positive on the right of the stationing direction". Therefore right edge of pavement = offset +12: LN-007 (T-1, y=988), AR-005 (C-1), LN-008 (T-2), AR-006 (C-2), LN-009 (T-3, y=1488).

Now, our stations of interest: 30+00, 31+20, 36+00 — all on T-2 (27+91.37 to 40+31.72).

T-2: from [2784.740127, 1061.580042] to [3961.444905, 1453.814968], length 1240.3557 ft, direction angle 18.4349° (east-northeast). Unit vector: dx = (3961.444905 - 2784.740127)/1240.355744 = 1176.704778/1240.355744. Let me compute: 1176.704778/1240.355744 ≈ 0.94870 (cos 18.435° = 0.9487). dy = (1453.814968 - 1061.580042)/1240.355744 = 392.234926/1240.355744 ≈ 0.31623 (sin 18.435° = 0.31623). Yes: cos(18.4349°) ≈ 0.94868, sin ≈ 0.31623. In fact tan = 392.2349/1176.7048 = 0.33333... Interesting: 392.234926/1176.704778 = exactly 1/3? 1176.704778/3 = 392.234926. Yes, exactly a 1:3 slope. So the direction is a 1:3 slope, length ratio: 12-5-13 triangle: cos = 12/13 = 0.92308? No wait. 392.2349/1176.7048 = 1/3. So dy/dx = 1/3, angle = arctan(1/3) = 18.4349°. Then cos = 3/√10 = 0.948683, sin = 1/√10 = 0.316228. Length = √(1176.7048² + 392.2349²) = 1176.7048 × √(1+1/9) = 1176.7048 × √(10/9) = 1176.7048 × 1.054093 = 1240.36. ✓

Right offset +12: perpendicular to the direction. Right of the direction of travel: for a direction angle θ (CCW from +x), the right normal is (sin θ, -cos θ). θ = 18.4349°, right normal = (0.316228, -0.948683). So a point at station s on T-2: centerline point P(s) = start + s'·(0.948683, 0.316228) where s' is the distance from T-2's start. Right edge point = P + 12×(0.316228, -0.948683) = P + (3.794734, -11.384197).

Verify: LN-008 (right edge of T-2) midpoint is at station 34+11.55 (station 3411.5453): centerline midpoint [3373.092516, 1257.697505]. Right edge point = [3373.092516 + 3.794734, 1257.697505 - 11.384197] = [3376.88725, 1246.313308]. And LN-008's reported point is [3376.8872, 1246.3133]. ✓

Now the design:
- Taper start (departure from existing right EP) is 30+00.
- Full width from 31+20 to 36+00: 12 ft wide (additional 12 ft to the right of the existing EP, i.e., at the full-width section the new EP is at offset +24).
- 120 ft straight taper: from 30+00 (offset +12) to 31+20 (offset +24). 31+20 - 30+00 = 120 ft. ✓ Straight taper, 12 ft lateral change over 120 ft.
- Full-width edge from 31+20 to 36+00 (at offset +24).
- Right-angle (perpendicular) end at 36+00, back to the existing EP (offset +12).

Since 30+00, 31+20, and 36+00 are all on the straight T-2 tangent, this is simple: everything is straight.

But the task says "draw the new edge of pavement on layer rd_EP — taper, full-width edge, and right-angle end at 36+00 to existing edge." Should I use draw_station_offset? It follows the alignment with arcs on curves, but here everything is on a straight tangent so it just draws straight lines. Actually, draw_station_offset with points ['30+00@12', '31+20@24', '36+00@24', '36+00@12'] draws exactly this: a taper (offset change = straight taper), a full-width segment at 24, and a right-angle end at 36+00 from 24 back to 12. That's a single call, and the entities are anchored to the design. That's the clean approach.

Wait, "existing edge of pavement" is offset +12 — the right side. Yes, the offset +12 chain (LN-007 etc.). "12 ft wide, full width from 31+20 to 36+00" — the right-turn lane is 12 ft wide, so from the existing EP (+12) to the new EP (+24).

Hmm, but should the right-angle end close back? If I include both '36+00@24' and '36+00@12' in draw_station_offset, the last segment is a right-angle cross-line (station is the same, offset changes). That gives a closed shape? No, not closed — 4 points: P1 (30+00@12), P2 (31+20@24), P3 (36+00@24), P4 (36+00@12). The polyline is open (close=false is default). That's the new EP: taper, full width, right-angle end. The segment P4 (36+00@12) ends right on the existing EP.

Alternatively, I could draw 3 separate lines. draw_station_offset is the design-integrated way and gets anchoring. Let me use that.

First let me compute the coordinates to report (I need to display the arithmetic anyway):

T-2 start: station 27+91.37 (2791.367473) is at point [2784.740127, 1061.580042].
Direction unit vector u = (0.948683, 0.316228) — more precisely: u = (cos θ, sin θ), tan θ = 1/3. cos θ = 3/√10 = 0.9486833, sin θ = 1/√10 = 0.3162278.
Right normal n = (sin θ, -cos θ) = (0.3162278, -0.9486833).

Station 30+00 = 3000. Distance from T-2 start: 3000 - 2791.367473 = 208.632527 ft.
Centerline at 30+00: [2784.740127 + 208.632527×0.9486833, 1061.580042 + 208.632527×0.3162278]
= 208.632527×0.9486833 = 197.9299... Let me compute: 208.632527 × 0.9486833 ≈ 208.632527 × 0.95 = 198.201 minus 208.632527×0.0013167 ≈ 0.2747 → 197.9265. More precisely: 208.632527 × 0.9486833:
208.632527 × 0.9 = 187.769274
208.632527 × 0.0486833 = 10.15682 (208.632527 × 0.05 = 10.431626; subtract 208.632527 × 0.0013167 = 0.27472 → 10.15691)
Total ≈ 197.92618.
y: 208.632527 × 0.3162278 ≈ 66.0 (208.632527 × 0.3162278: 208.632527 × 0.3 = 62.589758; 208.632527 × 0.0162278 = 3.38573; total 65.97549).
Centerline at 30+00 ≈ [2784.740127 + 197.92618, 1061.580042 + 65.97549] = [2982.666307, 1127.555532].

Hmm, let me do it exactly. Actually, T-2 direction is 1/3 slope and T-2 starts at station 2791.367473 at point (2784.740127, 1061.580042). The relationship: for a station s on T-2, distance from T-2 start d = s - 2791.367473. Centerline point = (2784.740127 + (12/√10)·d, 1061.580042 + (1/√10)·d).

For 30+00: d = 208.632527. (1/√10)·d = 208.632527 × 0.31622777 = 65.97548 (computing: 208.632527 × 0.31622777: 200 × 0.31622777 = 63.245554; 8.632527 × 0.31622777 = 2.729833; total 65.975387). x offset = 3 × that = 197.926161. So centerline: x = 2784.740127 + 197.926161 = 2982.666288; y = 1061.580042 + 65.975387 = 1127.555429.

Existing right EP at 30+00 (offset +12): add 12×n = (3.794733, -11.384199): [2986.461021, 1116.171230]. This is point P1, the departure.

Actually 12×0.31622777 = 3.7947333; 12×0.94868330 = 11.3841996.

P1 = 30+00@12 = [2986.461, 1116.171].

P2 = 31+20@24: station 3120, d = 3120 - 2791.367473 = 328.632527. (1/√10)d = 328.632527 × 0.31622777 = 103.925387 (208.632527 part = 65.975387; plus 120 × 0.31622777 = 37.947332; total 103.922719... wait: 65.975387 + 37.947332 = 103.922719). Hmm let me redo: 328.632527 × 0.31622777. 328.632527 × 0.31622777 = 300 × 0.31622777 = 94.868331; 28.632527 × 0.31622777 = 9.054473; total 103.922804. (1/√10)d = 808.632527 × 0.31622777 = 255.720135... computing: 808.632527 × 0.31622777: 800 × 0.31622777 = 252.982216; 8.632527 × 0.31622777 = 2.729833; total 255.712049. x offset = 767.136147. Centerline: [2784.740127 + 767.136147, 1061.580042 + 255.712049] = [3551.876274, 1317.292091]. Offset +24: P3 = [3559.465741, 1294.523692].

P4 = 36+00@12: centerline + 12×n = [3551.876274 + 3.794733, 1317.292091 - 11.384199] = [3555.671007, 1305.907892].

These are the coordinates I'll verify against what draw_station_offset returns (it should report the points, or I can find_entities the new entities and check).

Also check: does the full-width range 31+20 to 36+00 fit entirely within T-2 (which ends at 40+31.72)? Yes. And the taper starts at 30+00 > 27+91.37. Good, all straight.

Now, the tool: draw_station_offset with alignment SR-100, points ['30+00@12', '31+20@24', '36+00@24', '36+00@12'], layer rd_EP. Note the offset sign: positive = right. '12' means +12 (right). In the example, '15R' explicitly says right. '82+00@15R' etc. Plain numbers are positive = right, so I can use plain numbers, but for clarity I could write '30+00@12R'. The schema says offset in feet, positive right, and a string can include 'R'. For clarity let me use the explicit R notation: '30+00@12R', '31+20@24R', '36+00@24R', '36+00@12R'.

Should I set polyline=true to make it one polyline? The task says to draw the new edge of pavement: taper, full-width edge, right-angle end. Either as one polyline or as 3 separate lines. Either is fine. draw_station_offset's default is lines and arcs. 4 points, no curves (all on a straight) → 3 line segments. Should I use polyline: true? Hmm — a single polyline with arc segments; since it's all straight, just a 3-vertex polyline... Actually, 4 points → 3 segments. polyline=true makes one polyline. That's cleaner and easy to offset later. But anchoring: even a polyline keeps anchors. Either is fine. To match the existing EP style (separate lines per element, LN-007 etc.), I'll leave it at the default (separate lines) — actually, the existing EP is separate lines per tangent/curve. A 3-segment polyline would be one entity spanning the taper + full width + right angle. For a new EP, a single polyline is quite standard. But there's a risk: if I want to modify one part later, separate lines are easier. I'll go with the default (separate entities) — safest, and it matches the task's "taper, full-width edge, right-angle end" as 3 separate items.

Also: the full-width edge at +24 from 31+20 to 36+00 — should it "follow" the alignment? On a straight it's the same.

One more consideration: the taper "departs from the existing edge of pavement at station 30+00" — departs from the EP at 30+00 ✓, and is a "120 ft straight taper" — 30+00 to 31+20 is 120 ft ✓.

Let me do the draw_station_offset call.

Should I draw the lane line or the new edge — the task asks only for the EP. OK.

Let me execute the call.

messages.content: The geometry has been confirmed: the taper starts at (2986.46, 1116.17) on the existing EP, and the outer corner of the square end is at (3559.47, 1294.52). The entire region is on a straight tangent T-2, and since the existing right-side EP is at +12, the lane edge is at +24. Next, I'll draw the new EP as a station-and-offset polyline: a taper from 30+00@12 to 31+20@24, a full-width edge at 24 to 36+00, and then a perpendicular (square) end at 36+00 returning to the existing EP.
messages.reasoning:
Let me think about the geometry.

Existing right-side EP (edge of pavement): offset +12 from the alignment (LN-008 is the +12 offset of T-2, from station 2791.37 to 4031.72, passing through the whole region of interest).

Task: Add a right-turn lane on the right side, width 12 ft. Full width from station 31+20 to 36+00. Open with a straight 120-ft taper starting at 30+00 (30+00 + 120 ft = 31+20 ✓).

So the new EP (edge of the right-turn lane) is:
- From the existing EP (offset 12), start tapering at station 30+00.
- Taper runs from station 30+00 (offset 12) to station 31+20 (offset 24).
- Full-width edge at offset 24, from 31+20 to 36+00.
- At 36+00, a square end: a straight-line drop from offset 24 back to the existing EP at offset 12, i.e. a straight line perpendicular to the roadway ("square end").

The task says: "Draw the new edge of pavement on layer rd_EP — the taper, the full-width edge, and the square end at 36+00 back to the existing edge."

So what to draw:
1. Taper line: from (30+00 @ 12R) to (31+20 @ 24R).
2. Full-width edge: from (31+20 @ 24R) to (36+00 @ 24R).
3. Square end: from (36+00 @ 24R) to (36+00 @ 12R).

These can all be done in a single call using draw_station_offset: points ['30+00@12', '31+20@24', '36+00@24', '36+00@12'].

Wait — draw_station_offset follows the alignment when the offset is the same between consecutive points (default follow=true). 30+00@12 → 31+20@24 is a taper (straight line, since offset changes). 31+20@24 → 36+00@24 is the same offset so it follows the alignment exactly (here the alignment is a straight line T-2, so it's a straight line either way). 36+00@24 → 36+00@12 is same station, offset changes — straight line.

Note: offset sign — per convention, right is positive. "right positive" — meaning '31+20@24' means 24 ft to the right. The existing EP is at +12 (LN-008 offset 12). Good.

Should I close it? No — this task only asks for the new EP line: the taper, the full-width edge, and the square end. The existing EP line from 30+00 to 36+00 already exists (LN-008), so no closing is needed. So no close=true.

Let me use draw_station_offset with a polyline for a single continuous entity:

draw_station_offset {
  alignment: "SR-100",
  points: ["30+00@12", "31+20@24", "36+00@24", "36+00@12"],
  layer: "rd_EP",
  polyline: true
}
